newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan group calls for lifting ban on newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan group calls for lifting ban on newspaper.

text.p: Morocco's independent Human Rights Organisation (OMDH) on Thursday urged the government to urgently lift the ban imposed on one of the country's most popular newspapers, a spokesman said.
The interior ministry on Wednesday banned Al-Oussbou Assahafi Assiassi--a weekly political newspaper-- with no explanation, the group said.

"Given the progress seen over human rights issues in the World in recent years...We demand that (the government) urgently lift this ban on the newspaper which has been ordered with no motivation and no judicial guarantee," the OMDH said.
The ban, which came a few days after the national day for the press freedom, is disconcerting, the group said.
The newspaper's editor Mustapha Alaoui was summoned on Tuesday to police headquarters and informed that the Oussbou Assahafi Assiassi was banned in Morocco but gave no explanation.
The ban, which was signed by the Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali, was effective from November 20, 1996, he said.
In a statement sent to Reuters, the editor denounced the decision which he said ..."violates the freedom of speech and the basic principles of human rights in Morocco."
The independepent al-Oussbou Assahafi Assiassi, has a circulation of more than 100,000 copies per week.
Morocco has a dozen daily newspapers and four weekly papers, half of them published in Arabic and the remainder in French. Most are party mouthpieces.
